# Claude Code 2.1.317: editor-probe, freshness, M59 and parser-cost evidence

Measured on 2026-11-03 for PRD #1666 part 3's activation, on the executable with SHA-256 `eb224419e344575faa4a1f39b290b649425a10cd5ee2ef1d003480cd9ae57eb0`, the official `@anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64@2.1.317` (byte-identical to the host's installed copy). The screen and ring captures for the same release are under `../r5wake/` (`claude-2.1.317-*`, described in `../r5wake/claude-menu-candidates.md`). The editor-probe, M59 and freshness runs here were local lane-2 runs, in the TUI harness's own HOME, with every submission blocked by a private hook before a model turn. `parser-cost-replay.txt` is not a lane-2 run: it is the output of an `--ignored` unit replay in the release profile over the recorded traces, these included. The raw captures, PTY bytes included, stay in the `source_capture` directory each summary names under `/var/tmp` on the recording machine; these files are compact summaries of them.

## Recorders, and how the summaries are made

Each recorder is `tests/support/claude_editor_measure.py` (editor probe) or `tests/support/claude_helper_alarm_measure.py` (M59); a summary's `recorder_sha256` is the SHA-256 of the recorder file that made its capture, and each row above names the committed revision whose hash it carries. Each summary is written by `tests/support/claude_evidence_summary.py` from its capture's `result.json`; that script's docstring gives the field mapping, and `python3 -I tests/support/claude_evidence_summary.py --check <source_capture> <summary>` regenerates a summary and compares it byte for byte.

Every file in the table that names a recorder was rerun on 2026-11-03 with the committed recorder named beside it, replacing the summaries first committed in `4c5e519c`. Of those, four editor-probe files (`-089-forms-m44e`, `-088-keymap-start-m49b`, `-keymap-unchanged-m49b`, `-keymap-reload-m49b`) had come from an older editor recorder, `eb742c62…`, and `m59-090-armed-timeout` from an older M59 recorder, `1ca2804e…`. The older editor recorder's `reset` sent a second Escape after the first, which on an empty composer opens Rewind; the committed one sends a second Escape only while a dialog reads `Esc to cancel`. It also had a single project-keymap cell, where the committed one adds the cell launched with every settings source. The older M59 recorder differed only in the unarmed cell (its tenth press exited 37, where the committed one adds an eleventh), which the armed-timeout cell does not run. The committed M59 recorder (`bbacdcc3…`) adds Claude's notices split at the helper's end. The reruns read the same as the first summaries on every value a record would use: the same forms table, ESC/BEL gaps and pasted-BEL reading, the same export, selection and paste toggles, and the same keymap outcomes (start at 1.02–1.34 s, created effective by 3.75 s, removed by 2.53 s, project file no effect).

## Readings worth stating plainly

- **Pasted BEL is kept as text.** A bracketed `PASTE` BEL `TAIL` opened no editor (2/2, whole and split, in both the first run and the rerun), and the next export held `BASEPASTE\x07TAIL`: hex `424153455041535445075441494c`, the bytes the editor stand-in read from the file. That is what 2.1.310 did. The first measurement report said 2.1.317 *dropped* the BEL; it had read `composer_after`, the screen text, which reads `BASEPASTETAIL` because a BEL in the draft is not drawn. The committed summary was right and the report was wrong. The proposed record value stays `Absent`.
- **Paste toggles, by path.** One `?2004l` before the editor and one `?2004h` after it, 5/5 on the `VISUAL` path that the deck's helper is reached by, and asserted as that value. The `EDITOR` and PATH `vi` cells wrote the same; the PATH `code -w -g` fallback wrote no `?2004` at all.
- **M59 cell (a): SIGALRM seen directly in 10/10.** Claude's own notice `Dot-agent-deck-editor closed unexpectedly (SIGALRM)`, its reading of the wait status it reaped, appeared after the helper's end in every press and before it in none. The zombie's wait status was seen 0/10 in the rerun (1/10 in the first run): Claude usually reaps the helper before the 1 ms poll sees it. In every press the helper's trace ends at `pause ready` with no orderly exit, and it ended 5.0016–5.0061 s after its branch.
- **M59 row T** (armed, unanswered exchange; not an alarm pass): the trace ends `armed None ArmedExit { notice: true, status: 0 }` in 10/10, and the helper's notice reached the terminal 10/10. It ended 3.513–3.518 s after its branch, and the zombie, seen 2/10, exited 0.
- **M59 cell (b)**: unarmed branch, one editor run each, helper alive 10.12–10.14 s, trace `exit Status(0)` 10/10 with the sentinel reimported, and `exit Status(37)` on the eleventh press, where Claude's notice read `quit unexpectedly (exit code 37)` and the draft was kept.

## The blocked prompt's restore (the composer tests, `../r5wake/`)

The composer tests' recorder (`tests/support/claude_release_measure.py`) clears the composer after Claude puts the hook-blocked prompt back in it. The wait added in `4c5e519c` waited for the line's *text*, which in the replayed 24 × 80 runs did not leave the box (the submitted line stayed drawn `❯` and a plain space until the restore drew it `❯` and a no-break space), so it returned at once. A rerun failed when 2.1.317 restored one prompt 629 ms after the hook, after the clear, and replaying that run and three others showed the recorded times were not restore times (about 20 ms recorded at 24 × 80 against about 60 ms, and one 33 ms against 367 ms). The first measurement report's "max 302 ms / 34 ms (against 2.1.312's 313 / 33 ms)" came from that wait and does not stand. The recorder now waits for the submitted form and then for the editable draft, and the tests assert all fifteen restores were seen within the 5 s bound and print the largest. With it, on 2026-11-03, the largest restore after the hook was 742 ms (2.1.317, 50 × 200), 368, 674 and 513 ms (2.1.317, 24 × 80, three runs), 726 ms (2.1.312, 50 × 200) and 445 ms (2.1.312, 24 × 80), all passing; the committed `r5wake` composer fixtures are the first run's and were not replaced.

## For the 2.1.317 record's author

- `pasted_bel_is_text`: `Absent`, with the reconciled reading above in its comment.
- `paste_toggles`: say the value was measured on the `VISUAL` path, and that the PATH `code -w -g` fallback writes none.
- `parser_cost`: `src/doorbell_activation.rs`'s `RELEASE_RECORDS` doc comment says "at most 501 µs added to a push's lock hold and 5.0 ms of scanner CPU per generation". Restate it with this run's figures and their load context: 2.1.317's traces at most 1315.8 µs added hold and 10.95 ms per generation, with the aggregate p99 (213.9 µs), every push's maximum and every generation's CPU within plan §4.6's limits (on the smallest traces, 7 to 34 pushes at 80 × 300, the per-trace p99 reached 1.3 ms under this load, 2.1.317's own start trace 1251 µs), measured with a load average of 10.65 on 16 CPUs at the start, from other work on the box, with 2.1.312's rows in the same run of the same size (`parser-cost-replay.txt`).
- A-20d-7: land the record first, then rerun `probe_083` with `DAD_PROBE_FRESHNESS_RELEASE=2.1.317` against the committed build and append those lines; the test now writes the deck's `build_id` into each summary line.

## The record, and A-20d-7 against it

The 2.1.317 record landed in `bfc0e626` (`src/doorbell_activation.rs`), with the values above: its ring measurements verified as 2.1.312's, and its measured editor probe kept as `CLAUDE_2_1_317_EDITOR_PROBE` (paste toggles on the `VISUAL` path, `pasted_bel_is_text` `Absent`), which the record's `editor_probe` takes at activation. `probe_083` was then rerun on 2026-11-03 against the committed build `0.49.5-g11bc1f83`, on the host's installed 2.1.317 (the SHA-256 above), in the harness's own HOME: three idle runs and two with sixteen `yes` burners, lines 6–10 of `freshness-a20d7.jsonl`. All five passed. Of 350 probes outside the control, none was refused for freshness at the writer and none when scheduled, and every one was written: 40 per run at the production interval (round trip at most 21 ms), 15 held 100 ms and 15 held 1 s. The control refused 25 of 25 for the screen. The idle agent drew one 43-byte frame per minute's watch and no frame between probes. The box was shared with other work: the 1-minute load was 2.7–4.5 at the idle runs (the 15-minute up to 12.5) and about 18 under the burners, each sampled as its run ended (the summary line's `load` field), CPU pressure (`some avg10`) up to 14%, against at most 4.2% in the provisional runs. This matches the provisional lines.
